answer: In a market where AI agents arrange timber deliveries to a mountain ledge, every active bidder must lock $100 for 30 days, and each deposit permits one live bid. Creating aliases cannot multiply bidding power because the same deposit cannot back two bids. A sybil swarm of 1,000 bidders therefore ties up $100,000 for a month; the ripple of new identities brings a proportional capital and opportunity cost.
